hints: Equal elements never swap, so preserve their original order when sorting.
In a left-to-right round, an element can move left by at most one position.
The maximum stable leftward displacement determines the number of rounds.
analogy: A small element can pass only one larger neighbor per round as the scan moves away from it.
example: For [3,2,4,1,4], the 1 moves from position 4 to position 1, so three rounds are needed.
algorithm: Stable-sort pairs (value,original index), breaking ties by original index. For each sorted position j, compute originalIndex-j. Output the largest such displacement, or zero if the array is already sorted.
correctness: No element can move left more than one place in a single left-to-right scan, so its leftward displacement is a lower bound. In each round, every element that still has a larger element immediately before it moves left; equivalently stable inversions are eliminated at a rate sufficient to place every element after at most the maximum leftward displacement rounds. Thus the bound is attained.
complexity: For n elements, sorting takes O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
